If destination is a directory, the source file will be copied into the destination directory. So we can do cp source=TeamNotes.txt destination=Archived. That will copy into Archived/TeamNotes.txt. But we want IdeasArchive.txt. We can copy then rename? Or use mv? We can copy to Archived/TeamNotes.txt then rename to IdeasArchive.txt. Or we can use cp with destination=Archived/IdeasArchive.txt? The spec says no file paths allowed. So cannot include slash. So we must copy to Archived then rename. Let's do cp TeamNotes.txt Archived. Then mv Archived/TeamNotes.txt Archived/IdeasArchive.txt. But mv also requires source and destination local to current directory. So cannot specify path. So we can't move inside Archived. We might need to cd into Archived then copy? We can use cp with source=TeamNotes.txt destination=IdeasArchive.txt while in Archived? But source must be local to current directory. So cannot refer to parent. We need to copy into Archived. We can use cp with source=TeamNotes.txt destination=Archived. That copies into Archived/TeamNotes.txt. Then we can rename that file to IdeasArchive.txt.
